title: Pillars II: performance, cost, sustainability

kcs.statement: The performance efficiency pillar is about using computing resources efficiently as demand and technology change: democratise advanced technologies, go global in minutes, use serverless architectures and experiment more often.

The cost optimization pillar delivers business value at the lowest price: adopt a consumption model, measure overall efficiency, stop spending on undifferentiated heavy lifting, and analyse and attribute expenditure.
The sustainability pillar, added in 2021, minimises a workload's environmental impact: maximise utilisation, use managed services and adopt more efficient hardware and software.
Removing idle or oversized resources to cut spending maps to cost optimization, while choosing faster resource types or adding caching to cut latency maps to performance efficiency.

problem_ideas: A team wants to cut its carbon footprint by raising average server utilisation from 15% to 60%: which pillar?
Turning off dev environments every night and weekend: which pillar?
Choosing a GPU instance to cut model inference time from 2 s to 200 ms: which pillar?
Tagging resources by team to see who spends what: which pillar and which principle?
Two pillars both mention 'go global in minutes' in prep notes: which is the official home?
Sort ten scenarios across all six pillars, then explain the two you found hardest.
